verdicts.reading: Of the ~30 US battery factories planned, under construction or operating in mid-2024, 13 are open (operating) by the end of 2025. D30 state-of-affairs claim with a count, graded on the D16 numeric rule for levels/counts (hit within 10%).
verdicts.reason: Third-party question (D30): the edition (p. text checked in the archived PDF) states the figure in McKinsey's own voice ('are expected to open by 2025') with no footnote or attribution; the match to DOE's Dec-2021 list of 13 new gigafactories is grader A's inference, and the edition's frame (13 of ~30, incl. already-operational plants) is not the DOE frame (13 new plants). So it is the publisher's forecast, not a quoted figure. Measure (D23): the Dallas Fed (2026-03-03) counts the same quantity for the same scope - US battery gigafactories of the recent build-out: 12 operating and 23 under construction (35 total, consistent with the edition's ~30 frame). Different vintage/method of the same quantity is gradable under D23; only one public tally found, so no range test applies. Grader A's 'no public tally found' is superseded by this source, which grader B cited. Arithmetic: 13 forecast vs 12 actual, error 1/12 = 8.3% (B's '+8%' is correct) -> within 10% -> hit. Grader B's alternative DOE-list reading (miss) is less faithful because the edition does not cite or reproduce that list. Uncertainty: the Dallas Fed count is dated March 2026 rather than 31 Dec 2025 and does not state whether pre-2021 plants (e.g. Panasonic Nevada, AESC Smyrna, LGES Holland) are included; if they were added the operating count would be ~15 and the verdict would drop to partial (13 vs 15 = 13%).

evidence.title: McKinsey Technology Trends Outlook 2024, Future of mobility
evidence.shows: 'approximately 30 battery factories are currently planned, being constructed, or operational in the United States alone; 13 of them are expected to open by 2025.' No footnote or attribution on the sentence (checked in pdftotext of the archived PDF).

evidence.title: Dallas Fed, U.S. battery industry cuts losses, shifts to new ventures amid EV bust
evidence.shows: After 'several dozen new gigafactories in the U.S. have been announced in the past five years': '12 plants operating and another 23 are at various stages of construction'. No plant list or type split in the text.

evidence.title: Electrek, 13 battery gigafactories coming to the US by 2025
evidence.shows: DOE 2021 list of 13 new planned plants; possible origin of the number, but a different frame (13 new plants, not 13 of ~30) and not cited by the edition.
